picks.excerpt: Warner Bros. built a campaign for the Anne Hathaway/Ewan McGregor sci-fi film 'The End of Oak Street' around an AI-generated talking-dog podcast. A studio marketing department using generative video as a first-class promo format, not a test.
picks.rationale: A major studio shipping generative video as the centerpiece of a real theatrical campaign — the clearest signal yet of where AI video actually lands in a marketing brief.

picks.excerpt: Rich Young's monthly After Effects roundup covers the beta AI Assistant that automates physics animation and layer management via natural language, plus the third-party AI tools reshaping motion work. A survey of what actually shipped into AE this month.
picks.rationale: Most directly actionable pick — the AE AI Assistant beta and the tools around it change a motion designer's timeline work tomorrow, with no studio-scale prerequisites.

picks.excerpt: Roku has launched Fairground, a free ad-supported channel of fully AI-generated programming, and the viewing experience is grim. An early read on what happens when generative video is scheduled as linear television.
picks.rationale: First mainstream distributor to schedule all-AI programming as linear TV — a hands-on verdict on how generative video holds up at broadcast length, not clip length.

picks.excerpt: Gregg Araki, no fan of AI, describes the one place it earned its keep on 'I Want Your Sex': a specific editing problem he could not solve any other way. A concrete craft account rather than a position statement.
picks.rationale: An AI skeptic naming the exact edit-room problem the tools solved — a usable boundary line for directors deciding where AI belongs in post.

picks.excerpt: Portuguese auteur Edgar Pera discusses 'Asphalt Guerrilla,' premiering at Locarno, which blends fact, fiction and AI-generated imagery into a story about filmmaking. He explains how he uses AI as a craft tool precisely to argue against it.
picks.rationale: A festival premiere that uses generative imagery as authored material with a stated position — the rare case where the AI is the argument, not the shortcut.
